headline: 7 DU students injured after car hits them on campus
summary: The driver, the son of a DU teacher, claimed he accidentally pressed the accelerator instead of the brake while learning to drive.
details: At least seven Dhaka University students were injured after a car hit them on campus, with two students seriously injured and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The victims include six students from the Marketing Department and one from the Department of Linguistics. Zahid Hasan suffered a deep cut above his eye requiring five stitches, and Kaniz Fatema Adrita sustained a leg fracture.

The driver, identified as Shadman, is a student of DU's Institute of Information Technology and the son of Shahidul Islam, a teacher at the Department of Mathematics and former VC of Pirojpur Science and Technology University.

Shadman told students at the scene that it was his first time driving and he accidentally pressed the accelerator instead of the brake. University Proctor Israfil Ratan stated that the student had taken the car without his father's permission.
Following the incident, students vandalized the car and took the driver to the university proctor's office. He was later seen in the room of the officer-in-charge of Shahbagh Police Station.
University authorities are arranging to cover the treatment costs for the injured students. No formal police case has been filed yet, as students and authorities are discussing the matter.
caption:
A first-time driver hit 7 students on the DU campus, leaving two seriously injured.

At least seven Dhaka University students were injured after a car hit them on campus, with two students seriously injured and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The victims include six students from the Marketing Department and one from the Department of Linguistics. Zahid Hasan suffered a deep cut above his eye requiring five stitches, and Kaniz Fatema Adrita sustained a leg fracture.

The driver, identified as Shadman, is a student of DU's Institute of Information Technology and the son of Shahidul Islam, a teacher at the Department of Mathematics and former VC of Pirojpur Science and Technology University.

Shadman told students at the scene that it was his first time driving and he accidentally pressed the accelerator instead of the brake. University Proctor Israfil Ratan stated that the student had taken the car without his father's permission.

Following the incident, students vandalized the car and took the driver to the university proctor's office. He was later seen in the room of the officer-in-charge of Shahbagh Police Station.

University authorities are arranging to cover the treatment costs for the injured students. No formal police case has been filed yet, as students and authorities are discussing the matter.

headline_marked: [[Litton Das sets world record]] with 9 dismissals, century & half-century in same Test
headline: Litton Das sets world record with 9 dismissals, century & half-century in same Test
summary: Litton Das becomes the first wicketkeeper in Test history to achieve this feat on his 32nd birthday, surpassing a 1966 record. He also scored 53 and 102 runs.
details: On his 32nd birthday, Litton Das etched his name in cricket history by becoming the first wicketkeeper in Test matches to record nine dismissals while also scoring a century and a half-century in the same game. This remarkable achievement surpassed the previous record held since 1966.

The Bangladesh wicketkeeper-batter's historic feat occurred during the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi. Litton Das's performance was exceptional both behind the stumps and with the bat, contributing significantly to Bangladesh's effort.

Litton Das scored 53 runs in the first innings and followed it up with a brilliant 102 in the second innings. Behind the wickets, he took several crucial catches and completed a stumping, showcasing his all-round prowess.

His record-breaking ninth dismissal came from a spectacular one-handed catch off Ebadot Hossain, dismissing Ikram Alikhil. This catch was the final wicket to fall in Afghanistan's second innings, highlighting Litton's impact on the game.

Previously, Litton had set a Bangladesh record with eight dismissals in a single Test, breaking Khaled Mashud Pilot's record of seven. His consistent performance underscores his importance to the national team.

With nine dismissals in the match, Litton Das is now also closing in on the world record for most dismissals in a single Test, currently held jointly by Jack Russell, AB de Villiers, and Rishabh Pant with 11 dismissals.
